verses.1: And Josiah did a sacrifice to the LORD in Jerusalem. They sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.2: And the priests stood on their posts, strengthening them for the service in the house of Jehovah.
verses.3: And he said to the people who could understand: “To all the holy people of Jehovah, let them bring the Ark of the Covenant into the house that Solomon, son of David, king of Israel, built. Now, you have no strength to carry it on your shoulders. Therefore, worship Jehovah your God and the people of Israel.”
verses.4: And they made the house of your ancestors as if it were one of your own possessions, according to the writing of David, king of Israel, and according to the writing of Solomon, their son.
verses.5: And they stood in the Holy Place, in the section of the Tabernacle that belonged to our ancestors, the children of the people. This was also the section of the Tabernacle that belonged to the Levites.
verses.6: And they shall observe Passover, and become holy. They shall prepare it for their ancestors, so that they may do what the LORD has commanded through Moses.
verses.7: And Yosheiah ordered that the sheep of the people be slaughtered as sacrifices for Passover. All those sheep were used for this purpose. There were three hundred thousand sheep, and six hundred thousand cattle. These were all offerings from the king.
verses.8: And their priests served the people, as well as the priests and Levites. They offered sacrifices and offerings to remember him. The officials of the Temple gave away hundreds and six dozen cups during Passover.
verses.9: And Kananyahu, Shmaeyahu, Netanael his brothers, Hashbayahu, Yiayel, and Yozebad were the leaders of the Levites. They raised five thousand men for the festival of Pesach. In the morning, there were five hundred more men.
verses.10: And the service began. The priests stood in their positions, and the Levites stood on their posts, as commanded by the king.
verses.11: And they slaughtered the Passover animals. The priests threw them away, and the Levites scattered them over the ground.
verses.12: And they divided them into groups, according to the divisions mentioned in the Book of Moses. They offered them to Jehovah, as it was written there.
verses.13: And the Passover was sacrificed in flames, just as it should be. The offerings were placed in containers, and they were distributed among all the people.
verses.14: And after they were prepared for them and for the priests, since the priests, the sons of Aaron, prepared the offerings during the evening hours. And the libations were also prepared for them and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.
verses.15: And the scribes and scholars stood on their posts, according to David’s command. They gathered together, and they appointed leaders to govern the king. And in every door, there was no one to stop them from working, for their brothers, the Levites, had been prepared for this purpose.
verses.16: And all the sacrifices of Yahweh were to be offered on that day, as commanded by King Josiah.
verses.17: And the children of Israel did what was required of them at that time: they observed the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
verses.18: And there was never a Passover celebrated in Israel since the time of the prophet Samuel, nor by all the kings of Israel. They never celebrated the Passover that Joshua, the priests, the Levites, and all of Israel did. Nor did those who lived in Jerusalem do it either.
verses.19: In the eleventh year of King Josiah’s reign, this Passover was celebrated.
verses.20: After all this, Josiah prepared the house for use. Then he went up from Egypt to fight against Karkemish on the banks of the River Euphrates. And he went out to call upon Josiah.
verses.21: And they sent servants to him, saying, “What do you want? You are no longer king of Judah. Today I will go into battle against my enemies. God said to me, ‘Stop fighting against those who are with me.’ Do not let them destroy you.”
verses.22: And Yosheiah did not turn his face away from him, because he was ready to fight against him. He also did not listen to the words of God. So he went out to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
verses.23: And the soldiers went to see King Josiah. The king said to his servants, “Take me away, for I have sinned many times.”
verses.24: And his servants carried him down from the chariot. They placed him on the new chariot that belonged to him. Then they sent him to Jerusalem. He died there, and he was buried with his ancestors and all of the Jews. Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
verses.25: And Jeremiah wrote down all the complaints and grievances of the people against Yosia. He recorded them as laws for the Israelites. Those laws are still written down in the records.
verses.26: And the additional words of Josiah and his kindnesses are written in the laws of Jehovah.
verses.27: And their earlier and later words are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
